clue.text: Not prepared to be rebuffed on pay campaign

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another comes after it

parts.note: pay means wage

indicators.note: rebuffed, beaten back, says the word for not prepared is read backwards

parts.note: raw food is not prepared or cooked

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to be turned away in a campaign for better pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not prepared' looks like reluctance but means uncooked, and 'campaign' is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To wage war is to campaign, conduct a military operation, so the verb phrase fits.

clue.text: Branches suggesting depression hanging over bank?

definitions.text: Branches suggesting depression hanging over bank?

parts.words: Branches suggesting depression hanging over bank?
parts.note: a tree whose drooping boughs look sad, as if crying, leaning over a riverbank

explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' sounds like a dip or recession but means sadness, the tree's name suggesting tears.
explanation.definitionFit: This tree has drooping branches and often grows on riverbanks, looking as though it were crying.

clue.text: Messenger concealing cheese in wrap pipes up

indicators.note: concealing says the reversed word hides the cheese inside it
up in a down clue says the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to lag pipes is to wrap them in insulation
Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A courier hides some cheese in the insulation of pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAG into GAL, which then holds BRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is the archangel who brings messages from God, as in the Annunciation.

clue.text: It hurts to split couple getting excited

indicators.note: to split says the cry goes into the middle of the word for couple

parts.note: to couple is to join, to wed
ow is the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: A painful break-up leaves a couple upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' looks like a noun but is the verb wed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wowed has been thrilled or greatly impressed, so stirred up and excited.

clue.text: Settling right in, got so agitated

indicators.note: agitated says these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone settles right in, though got so agitated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges INGOTSO into OOSTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds roosting are settling down to rest on a perch.

clue.text: Chewed while holding dry fork

indicators.note: holding says the word for chewed contains the word for dry

parts.note: bit, as in 'the dog bit the bone', means chewed
sec is the French word for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: Someone chews food while gripping a dry fork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fork' looks like cutlery but is a verb: to split in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two parts, just as a road forks into two branches.

clue.text: Bar for impact serving large drink

definitions.meaning: the bar on a car that takes a collision
a glass filled to the brim, a big drink

explanation.definitionFit: It is both the car's protective bar and a brimming glass of drink.

clue.text: Little time employed in scoffing vegetable

indicators.note: employed in says these letters are put inside the word for scoffing

parts.note: scoffing at something is treating it with scorn
wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Little time is spent wolfing down vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffing' suggests eating greedily but here means mocking, SCORN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetcorn is maize eaten as a vegetable, the kernels cooked on or off the cob.

clue.text: Indian making sweet melt for Irishman

parts.note: a choc, chocolate, is a sweet

indicators.note: for Irishman says the word is said in an Irish accent, which turns th into t

parts.note: to thaw is to melt

explanation.surface: A chocolate is melted to give to an Irishman.
explanation.walkthrough: In a stage Irish accent 'thaw' is said like TAW.
explanation.definitionFit: The Choctaw are a Native American people, Indian in the old sense.

clue.text: Freedom to move barge back to dock

parts.note: to barge through a crowd is to elbow your way

indicators.note: back says the word for dock is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to moor a boat is to dock it

explanation.surface: Moving a barge back into its dock needs plenty of space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barge' looks like a boat in this picture but is the verb to shove. 'back' turns MOOR into ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is space enough to move freely, the idiom for freedom of movement.

clue.text: Return to finish off old live "network"

indicators.note: Return says the three pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: KO, a knockout, finishes off a boxer
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: An old live network is being brought back to be shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' turns KOOBE into EBOOK. The definition is a pun: a book read on screen is literally a work of the net.
explanation.definitionFit: Read playfully as net-work, it names a written work delivered electronically, a digital book.

clue.text: Are wise wives filling hot wash tank afresh?

indicators.note: afresh says these letters are rearranged anew

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife, so wives gives two

explanation.surface: Wives fill the hot wash tank again.
explanation.walkthrough: The two W's fill the anagram of HOTWASHTANK at separate points.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who are worldly-wise and in the know understand how things really stand.

clue.text: I competed with climber

parts.note: vied means competed

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having entered a contest alongside a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' is not a mountaineer but a climbing plant, ivy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered with the climbing plant ivy is described as ivy-clad, overgrown with that creeper.

clue.text: New totty with well-shaped figure

indicators.note: well-shaped says the letters are formed into a new shape

explanation.surface: A new attractive person has a shapely figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-shaped' rearranges NEWTOTTY plus W. 'totty' is British slang for attractive people; 'figure' here means a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a number written in digits, and this is the number after twenty-one.

clue.text: Source of wealth, or type of bomb

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a mine is an explosive device, a kind of bomb

explanation.surface: Something is either a source of riches or an explosive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link word but is the heraldic colour gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold mine, literally or figuratively, is anything yielding great riches.

clue.text: Why not for the whole of spring

definitions.meaning: a shrug of agreement, there is no reason against it
spring is March, April and the fifth month too, not just the first two

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means there is no reason not to, and spring includes the fifth month too.

clue.text: Bark has black web concealing separate rings

indicators.note: concealing says the black-and-web letters hide a ring inside them

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black

indicators.note: separate says one ring splits the web letters apart, going in between them

parts.note: WWW, the World Wide Web, is the web
a ring is round like the letter O
a second ring, another O

explanation.surface: Tree bark carries a dark spider's web hiding rings.
explanation.walkthrough: The two rings go in at separate places: one breaks up the web letters, the other sits after the B, giving B-O-W-W-O-W.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's bark is imitated as this childish sound of a dog's woof.

clue.text: Blow to back sends Tina wild

indicators.note: sends, as in sends crazy, says these letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A blow on the back sends Tina into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sends' rearranges TINAWILD.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind blowing from behind a moving craft pushes it along, a blow to its back.

clue.text: Hip's pierced by stake — gets embedded

definitions.note: a noun sense read as what gets embedded: pieces set into a surface

indicators.note: pierced by says the word for stake goes inside the word for hip's

parts.note: hip means fashionable, in; with the 's that gives in's
a lay can be a stake or bet

explanation.surface: A hip is pierced by a stake that lodges in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Hip's is IN + S, with LAY inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Inlays are decorative pieces set into wood or metal, so they are what gets embedded.

clue.text: Dance hit — turn up a touch

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard

indicators.note: turn up in a down clue says the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a dab is a light touch

explanation.surface: A dance hit makes everyone turn up and touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses ADAB to BADA.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast Brazilian dance popular around 1990.

clue.text: Cream filling pail on game-show overturned

indicators.note: overturned says the hidden letters are read backwards
filling says the answer is found inside the words that follow, as a filling sits inside a pie

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bucket of cream filling is knocked over on a TV game show.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Cream filling' as the definition, but 'filling' is needed to signal the letters inside 'pail on game', so the definition is just 'Cream'; 'overturned' then reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnolia is a creamy off-white paint colour, named after the flower.

clue.text: Deception about alcoholic drink being soft one

definitions.note: one stands for drink, so a soft one is a soft drink

indicators.note: about says the word for deception goes round the drink

parts.note: a lie is a deception
mead is an alcoholic drink of fermented honey

explanation.surface: A lie about an alcoholic drink pretending it is soft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to drink: a soft drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Limeade is a non-alcoholic drink flavoured with lime juice.

clue.text: Case involves court looking up notes from fifties

indicators.note: looking up in a down clue says the whole is read from the bottom up
involves says the case wraps around the word for court

parts.note: a pod is a seed case
to court someone is to woo

explanation.surface: A legal case involves a court looking into notes from the fifties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' and 'court' suggest a law court, but court here is the verb to woo, and the whole is read upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Doo-wop is a vocal harmony style of music from the 1950s.

clue.text: Angel so low flying brings warm coat

parts.note: lamb and angel are both terms of endearment

indicators.note: flying says these letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: An angel flying low brings a warm coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges SOLOW into SWOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambswool is soft wool from young sheep, a warm fleece or garment.

clue.text: Help us to capture a minute island

indicators.note: to capture says the distress call holds the other letters inside

parts.note: SOS is the distress call asking for help

explanation.surface: A plea for help to seize a tiny island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' reads as tiny but is the abbreviation M.
explanation.definitionFit: Samos is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean Sea.

clue.text: Brand carries weight and promise

indicators.note: carries says the word for brand holds the other letter

parts.note: to brand with hot iron is to sear

explanation.surface: A brand bears weight and makes a pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' puts W inside SEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to promise solemnly, to vow.

clue.text: Maybe humpback bridge team crosses ends in rough sea wall

indicators.note: crosses says the bridge team spans the other letters

parts.note: West and East are partners at bridge, a team

indicators.note: ends in picks the last letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A humpback bridge crosses the ends of a rough sea wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'humpback bridge' looks like a phrase, but 'Maybe humpback' is the definition and 'bridge team' means West and East, partners at the card game bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The humpback is one example of this large sea mammal, hence the 'Maybe'.

clue.text: A hiding of the worst kind?

definitions.text: A hiding of the worst kind?

parts.words: A hiding of the worst kind?
parts.note: a hiding is a thrashing, and the worst kind is a defeat in every game; also a hiding of the truth, a cover-up

explanation.walkthrough: In sport a series lost in every match is said to be this; it also means glossing over faults.
explanation.definitionFit: A series lost without a single win is a total thrashing, and the word also means a cover-up.

clue.text: Beer or punch

definitions.meaning: a slang word for beer or ale

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for beer and also a hard blow with the fist.

clue.text: English runner suffered when French one pulled out

indicators.note: pulled out says the French one is removed from the word for suffered

parts.note: underwent means suffered or experienced
un is French for one

explanation.surface: An English athlete suffered when the French one withdrew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is not an athlete but a river; the Derwent flows in several English counties.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a runner in crosswords, and the Derwent is a river in England.
